Original text: ADR-001 keeps sessions in memory (DEC-018), so simple-login.integration.2's restart stays a valid expired-token stand-in for AC-2.3 and the intake record's 'revisited if ADR-001's update makes sessions survive a restart' does not fire. The PRD v2 Success test that a restart keeps every booking must sign in again after the restart, since the same restart signs every user out (ADR-001 Consequences).

Carried from Q-040 (from S11, itself carried from Q-015, from S04), which matched S15 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a citation touch changes only citations (DEC-133). Original text: ADR-002 for the integration plan: the browser tests run with the browser's time zone set to a zone that is neither account's nor UTC (for example Asia/Kolkata, +05:30); the change-day tests take the next last Sunday of March and of October after the real clock, never a fixed date (2026-10-25 has passed; the next is 2027-03-28), and booking-api@v1's how-far-ahead limit decides whether that day is bookable through the API; the backend's clock decides 'started', which an end-to-end test cannot set, so the plan says which scripted test covers AC-5.5 and AC-6.2's started case (PRD v2 Success); the strings to assert are ADR-002 item 7's, including '23:00 to Fri 6 Nov 02:00' and '01:30 BST' / '01:30 GMT'.

Carried from Q-041 (from S11, itself carried from Q-020, from S05), which matched S15 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a citation touch changes only citations (DEC-133). Original text: booking-api@v1 for the integration plan: the 365-day horizon keeps the next London clock-change day bookable through the API under the real clock (at most 217 days ahead from any moment, hsdd/auto/experiments/booking-api-fixtures/). PRD v2 Success's 20 simultaneous attempts must give exactly one 201 and nineteen 409 BOOKING_CONFLICT naming the winner (G5, G6); a restart keeps every booking and id but drops tokens, so the test signs in again (G17). The fixtures carry a fixed clock and seeded state that the real service under the real clock cannot reproduce: only the 14 that depend on neither (the eight 400s, the four 401s, cancel-unknown and cancel-malformed-id) can be replayed exactly through the proxy; the stateful criteria are this node's own tests. consumers names simple-login.integration.3 provisionally (DEC-053).

Carried from Q-042 (from S11, itself carried from Q-021, from S06), which matched S15 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a citation touch changes only citations (DEC-133). Original text: auth-api@v1 now states the restart in the contract: G3, a restart of the service ends every token issued before it, and each is then rejected exactly as an expired token is (ADR-001, sessions kept in memory by DEC-018). The AC-2.3 expired-token stand-in (a backend restart) therefore stays valid and can cite auth-api@v1 G3 with profile-api@v2's same-401 guarantee; PRD v2 Success's restart test signs in again after the restart and finds every booking (booking-api@v1 G17). G2 now names booking-api@v1: a token from POST /api/login works at its four endpoints until expiresAt. G4: there is no logout endpoint; sign-out discards the token on the client.

Carried from Q-043 (from S11, itself carried from Q-024, from S07), which matched S15 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a citation touch changes only citations (DEC-133). Original text: The root's success criteria now follow PRD v2 Success only (DEC-073): 20 simultaneous attempts give one booking; every acceptance criterion passes in a scripted test, London's clock-change days included; a restart keeps every booking. PRD 1's 'Home within 3 seconds of Sign in' is gone. It is still asserted by the shipped simple-login.integration.1 (its Scope names 'the PRD's success metric') in e2e/login.spec.ts ('AC-1.1: the right password reaches Home within 3 seconds'). That phase is history; the integration node's touch (H9) should not name the 3-second check as a PRD criterion, and its appended plan decides whether a new phase keeps the assertion as a regression check or drops it.

Carried from Q-045 (from S11), which matched S15 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a citation touch changes only citations (DEC-133). Original text: From S11's touch (DEC-099 to DEC-102). Owns now says the root package.json scripts run the real service with its PostgreSQL 17, started through simple-login.backend's Docker Compose service, beside the real web app; the database, the Compose service and its Compose file stay the backend's (DEC-081), and where the file lives is H14's choice (Q-031). The shipped rig starts no database: scripts/dev.mjs and e2e/fixtures.ts spawn backend/src/server.ts directly, and the README's run instructions name no Docker or Colima. Bookings now persist across runs of the suite, so a test that books a slot computed from the clock can meet an earlier run's booking (a second run's 20 simultaneous attempts would then all get 409); the plan decides how a test run gets a database of its own or clean slots, through the backend's Compose service or booking-api@v1; writing the backend's tables directly would tie this node to a schema simple-login.backend owns. The Isolation strategy now runs the browser in a time zone that is neither account's nor UTC (ADR-002), which the plan's Playwright configuration sets, and says the service runs on the real clock. The Overview leaves to this plan which scripted test covers a booking that has started (PRD v2 AC-5.5, AC-6.2; DEC-102): asking for a started time works through the API under the real clock, but a booking of one's own that has started appears only by waiting for its start.
